examples.dm: There is no form, no feeling, no perception, and no intention; Within those, there is not even an atom's worth of a station for consciousness. They do not dwell on any phenomena, but practice without a dwelling place; Without grasping, they attain the awakening of the Sugatas.
examples.gm: There is no form, no feeling, no perception, and no volition; Consciousness does not dwell in them even slightly. Not dwelling in all phenomena, they practice without dwelling, And without grasping, they attain the awakening of the Sugatas.
examples.sa: न च रुप वेदन न संज्ञ न चेतना च विज्ञान स्थानु अणुमात्र न भोन्ति तस्य । सो सर्वधर्म-अस्थितो अनिकेतचारी अपरीरिगृहीत लभते सुगतान बोधिम् ॥

examples.dm: If, while dedicating, the notion of a mind arises, Or the notion of enlightenment, or the notion of sentient beings, Then because of such notions, one dwells in views and the mind is attached to the three; Because there is an object of observation, it is not a perfect dedication.
examples.gm: If, when dedicating, the notion of 'mind' arises, If there is the notion of awakening, the notion of dedicating, and the notion of sentient beings, Because of these notions, residing in views, the mind is attached to the three; Since there are apprehensions, it does not amount to dedication.
examples.sa: परिणामयन्तु यदि वर्तति चित्तसंज्ञा तथ बोधिसत्त्वपरिणामन सत्त्वसंज्ञा । संज्ञाय दृष्टिस्थितु चित्त त्रिसङ्गयुक्तो परिणामितं न भवती उपलभ्यमानम् ॥

examples.dm: Any bodhisattva who, while practicing in the past, Practiced this perfection skillfully and without doubt, Will, upon hearing this, immediately perceive it as the Teacher, And will quickly realize the peace of awakening.
examples.gm: When a bodhisattva practiced previously, The wise one practicing this perfection has no doubt. As soon as they hear it, they give rise to the notion of the Teacher; They will swiftly realize peaceful awakening.
examples.sa: यो बोधिसत्त्व वरपारमितेति चीर्णो परिचारिका य न च काङ्क्षति पण्डितेहि । सह श्रुत्व तस्य पुन भेष्यति शास्तृसंज्ञा सो वा लघू अनुबुधिष्यति बोधि शान्ताम् ॥

examples.dm: Wisdom is the precursor to the practice of generosity, And likewise for ethical discipline, patience, diligence, and meditative concentration. It is the total sustainer that prevents virtuous qualities from being lost; This demonstrates the single nature of all phenomena.
examples.gm: Wisdom is what precedes giving; Ethical discipline, patience, joyous effort, and concentration are likewise. In order that virtuous dharmas are not wasted, it fully upholds them. This demonstrates all dharmas as having a single way.
examples.sa: पूर्वंगमा भवतु दानु ददन्तु प्रज्ञा शीले च क्षान्ति तथ वीर्य तथैव ध्याने । परिग्राहिका कुशलधर्म-अविप्रणाशे एका च सा अपि निदर्शयि सर्वधर्मान् ॥

examples.dm: Pure and wearing clean robes, they are pure in the three isolations; They do not desire gain, and like great bulls, they always long for the Dharma. They have transcended the realm of Māra and are not dependent on others; They meditate on the four concentrations, yet do not dwell within those concentrations.
examples.gm: Making themselves clean and wearing clean clothes, the three are isolated and pure; Without desire for gain, the supreme leaders always desire the dharma. Passed beyond the realm of Māra and not placing themselves under the control of others, Meditating on the four dhyānas, they do not abide in those dhyānas.
examples.sa: शुचिशौचअम्बरधरा त्रिविवेकशुद्धा न च लाभकाम वृषभा सद धर्मकामाः । मारस्यतीतविषया अपरप्रणेया चतुध्यानध्यायि न च निश्रित तत्र ध्याने ॥

examples.dm: So too, the bodhisattva who has gone to the jewel island of emptiness, Having attained the meditative concentrations, faculties, and powers, Does not take delight in merely touching nirvana alone, And does not leave the suffering of sentient beings behind.
examples.gm: Likewise, a bodhisattva who has gone to the jewel island of emptiness, And attained the powers of the faculties of concentration, Does not merely delight in touching nirvāṇa, And leave sentient beings in suffering.
examples.sa: एमेव शून्यत व्रजित्वन रत्नद्वीपं लब्ध्वान ध्यान बल इन्द्रिय बोधिसत्त्वो । किंचापि निर्वृति स्पृशेदभिनन्दमानो अपि सर्वसत्त्व दुखिता मनसी भवन्ति ॥

examples.dm: If, while lacking such knowledge, one perceives form, And engages with the aggregates of feeling, volition, and consciousness, Even if one conceptualizes that "these aggregates are empty," that bodhisattva Is still practicing with signs and lacks faith in the state of non-arising.
examples.gm: If, lacking understanding, one perceives form, And practices regarding the aggregates of feeling, volition, and consciousness, Even if they think "these aggregates are empty," the bodhisattva Practices in signs, and does not have faith in the unborn state.
examples.sa: सचि रुप संज्ञ अपि वेदन चेतना च विज्ञान स्कन्ध चरती अप्रजानमानो । इमि स्कन्ध शून्य परिकल्पयि बोधिसत्त्वो चरती निमित्तअनुपादपदे असक्तो ॥

examples.dm: Permanent and impermanent, happiness and suffering, pleasant and unpleasant, Self and selflessness, suchness and likewise emptiness; One does not dwell in the attainment of the fruit or the stage of an arhat, Nor does one dwell in the stage of a pratyekabuddha or likewise the stage of a buddha.
examples.gm: Permanent and impermanent, happiness and suffering, attractive and unattractive, Self and selflessness, suchness and likewise emptiness, Attaining the fruit, and not abiding in the level of an arhat, Not abiding in the level of a pratyekabuddha, and likewise not in the level of a buddha.
examples.sa: नित्यम् अनित्यसुखदुःखशुभाशुभं ति आत्मन्य् अनात्मि तथता तथ शून्यतायाम् । फलप्राप्तिताय अथितो अरहन्तभूमौ प्रत्येकभूमिस्थितो तथ बुद्धभूमौ ॥

examples.dm: Thus the bodhisattvas practice the wisdom of the Victors; They know that these aggregates are empty and unborn from the very beginning. While not in meditative equipoise, they engage in compassion for the realm of sentient beings, And even during that interval, they never decline from the Buddha-dharma.
examples.gm: A bodhisattva engaging in the victors' perfection of wisdom, Knows these aggregates to be empty from the beginning and unarisen; Without resting in meditative equipoise, they enter into compassion for the realm of beings, And in the meantime, they never decline from the buddha dharmas.
examples.sa: पुन बोधिसत्त्व चरमाणु जिनान प्रज्ञां अनुपाद स्कन्ध इमि जानति आदिशून्यान् । असमाहितो करुण प्रेक्षति सत्त्वधातुम् अत्रान्तरे न परिहायति बुद्धधर्मान् ॥

examples.dm: There is no form, no feeling, no perception, and no intention; Within those, there is not even an atom's worth of a station for consciousness. They do not dwell on any phenomena, but practice without a dwelling place; Without grasping, they attain the awakening of the Sugatas.
examples.gm: There is no form, no feeling, no perception, and no volition; Consciousness does not dwell in them even slightly. Not dwelling in all phenomena, they practice without dwelling, And without grasping, they attain the awakening of the Sugatas.
examples.sa: न च रुप वेदन न संज्ञ न चेतना च विज्ञान स्थानु अणुमात्र न भोन्ति तस्य । सो सर्वधर्म-अस्थितो अनिकेतचारी अपरीरिगृहीत लभते सुगतान बोधिम् ॥

examples.dm: One who does not dwell in form, does not dwell in feeling, One who does not dwell in perception, does not dwell in volition, And one who does not dwell in consciousness, dwells in the nature of reality; This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Whoever does not abide in form, does not abide in feeling, Whoever does not abide in perception, does not abide in volition, And whoever does not abide in consciousness, abides in the nature of phenomena; This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: रुपस्मि यो न स्थिहते न च वेदनायां संज्ञाय यो न स्थिहते न च चेतनायाम् । विज्ञानि यो न स्थिहते स्थितु धर्मतायां एषा स प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: When one whose conduct is completely pure does not engage with form, And does not engage with consciousness, perception, feeling, or intention, Practicing in that way, they completely abandon all attachments, And, liberated from attachment, they practice the wisdom of the Sugatas.
examples.gm: Whoever, with perfectly pure conduct, does not practice in form, And does not practice in consciousness, perception, feeling, and volition, Practicing like that, entirely abandoning all attachment, Liberated from attachment, they practice the wisdom of the Sugatas.
examples.sa: रूपस्मि यो न चरते परिशुद्धचारी विज्ञान संज्ञ अपि वेदन चेतनायाम् । एवं चरन्तु परिवर्जयि सर्वसङ्गां सङ्गाद् विमुच्य चरते सुगतान प्रज्ञाम् ॥

examples.dm: When wise and learned bodhisattvas, contemplating non-arising, Practice in this way, Though they generate great compassion, they have no perception of sentient beings; This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Whenever a wise, understanding bodhisattva Reflects on non-arising and practices in this way, Generating great compassion without the perception of sentient beings, This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: यस्मिंश् च कालि समये विदु बोधिसत्त्वो एवं चरन्तु अनुपादु विचिन्तयित्वा । महतीं जनेति करुणां न च सत्त्वसंज्ञा एषा स प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: For one who has no perception of a self or perception of a sentient being, And whose perceptions are free from attachment, how could there be a lack of restraint? One who has no conceit regarding restraint or lack of restraint— This is what the Guide has called the restraint of morality.
examples.gm: Whoever has no perception of self and no perception of sentient beings, Being free from attachment to perceptions, how could they have non-restraint? Whoever has no conceit regarding restraint and non-restraint, This was taught by the Guide to be the discipline of restraint.
examples.sa: यस्यो न अस्ति अहसंज्ञ न सत्त्वसंज्ञा संज्ञाविरागु कुतु तस्य असंवरोऽस्ति । यस्यो न संवरि असंवरि मन्यनास्ति अयु शीलसंवरु प्रकाशितु नायकेन ॥

examples.dm: If one gives rise to the perception of sentient beings or the perception of suffering, Thinking, "I shall act for the benefit of beings and eliminate their suffering," One is a bodhisattva who conceptualizes a self and sentient beings; This is not the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: If they generate the perception of sentient beings and the perception of suffering, Thinking, "I shall act for the benefit of beings and eliminate their suffering," They are a bodhisattva who conceptualizes self and sentient beings; This is not the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: सचि सत्त्वसंज्ञ दुखसंज्ञ उपादयाती हरिष्यामि दुःख जगतीं करिष्यामि अर्थम् । सो आत्मस(त्त्व) परिकल्पकु बोधिसत्त्वो न च एष प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: The first chapter teaches omniscience of all aspects. Whatever rivers flow here in Jambudvīpa, Producing flowers, fruits, medicinal plants, and forests, All depend upon the Naga King, the Lord of Nagas, who dwells in Anavatapta; They are the power and glory of that Lord of Nagas.
examples.gm: Chapter One: The Teaching on the Knowledge of All Aspects. However many rivers flow in this Jambudvīpa, Producing flowers, fruits, medicinal herbs, and forests, All depend upon the nāga king, the lord of nāgas, dwelling in Anavatapta; It is the majestic power of that lord of nāgas.
examples.sa: यावन्ति नद्य प्रवहन्ति ह जम्बुद्वीपे फल पुष्प औषधाधि वनस्पति रोहयन्ति । भूजत गजेन्द्रनागपतिनिश्रयनोवतनस्य तस्यानुभावश्रिय साभु जगाधिपस्य ॥

examples.dm: For example, although there are billions of trees in the world of Jambudvīpa, In many various forms, with diverse colors and diverse shapes, Aside from speaking of them in terms of the number of things that cast a shadow, The shadows themselves are not diverse, nor is there any distinction between them.
examples.gm: For example, in Jambudvīpa there are thousands of tens of millions of trees, Of various kinds, numerous types, and many forms; Except when spoken of as a number of shadows, There are no various shadows, nor are there differences.
examples.sa: यथ जम्बुद्वीपि बहुवृक्षसहस्रकोटी नानाप्रकार विविधाश्च अनेकरूपाः । न वि छायनानतु भवेत विशेषतापि अन्यत्र छायगतसंख्य प्रभाषमाणा ॥

examples.dm: For example, if the Lord of Nagas were not present in Lake Anavatapta, How could the rivers ever flow here in Jambudvīpa? If there were no rivers, flowers and fruits would not grow, And the great ocean, too, would lack its many precious forms.
examples.gm: For example, if there were no nāga lord at Lake Anavatapta, How could rivers flow here in Jambudvīpa? If there were no rivers, flowers and fruits would not emerge, And the ocean would also not have many forms of jewels.
examples.sa: यथ नोपतप्त असतो भुजगाधिपस्य कुत नद्यप्रस्रवु भवेदिह जम्बुद्वीपे । असता नदीय फलपुष्प न संभवेयुः न च सागराण रतना भवि नैकरूपाः ॥

examples.dm: From the time they first generate the aspiration for supreme enlightenment, Until the time the true Dharma of those guides is exhausted, Whatever merit those Victors possess during that interval, Including the perfections and all the Buddha-qualities,
examples.gm: From when they first generated the mind for supreme awakening, Until the time the holy dharma of those Guides is exhausted, Whatever merit those Victors have during that time, And whatever is endowed with the perfections and whatever buddha-dharmas—
examples.sa: प्रथमं उपादु वरबोधयि चित्तुपादो यावत् सु धर्मक्षयकालु विनायकानाम् । एकस्मि तत्र चिय तेष जिनान पुण्यं सह युक्त पारमित येऽपि च बुद्धधर्माः ॥

examples.dm: Likewise, those who have truly entered into supreme awakening should understand that by hearing This Perfection of Wisdom of the Victors, Even if they have not received a direct prophecy from the Guide, "Before long, I shall touch the awakening of a Buddha."
examples.gm: Likewise, one who has fully entered supreme enlightenment Should be known as hearing this perfection of wisdom of the Victors; Even if they have not been directly prophesied by the Leaders, They think, 'Before long, I will touch the enlightenment of the Buddhas.'
examples.sa: एमेव बोधिवरप्रस्थितु वेदितव्यो श्रुणमाण प्रज्ञ इमि पारमिता जिनानाम् । यद्यापि संमुख न व्याकृतु नायकेनो तथपि स्पृशिष्यति नचिरेण हु बुद्धबोधिम् ॥

examples.dm: Those qualities from which the virtues of certain awakening arise— This is the meaning of ethical discipline for those endowed with virtuous qualities. The complete degeneration of the awakening of those who perform beneficial dharmas— This is what the Guide has called "immoral conduct."
examples.gm: Whatever dharmas produce the qualities of definite awakening, This is the purpose of discipline for those endowed with virtuous dharmas. Whatever dharmas cause the awakening of benefactors to completely degenerate, This was taught by the Guide to be broken discipline.
examples.sa: यो धर्म बोधिगुणआगमु सूरतानां सो शीलअर्थु गुणधर्मसमन्वितानाम् । यो धर्म बोधिगुणहानि हितंकराणां दुःशीलता अयु प्रकाशितु नायकेन ॥

examples.dm: Establishing the highest joy, respect, and faith, Having cleared away the obscurations of the afflictions and transcended all stains, Listen to this perfection of wisdom of the noble ones, who are dedicated to the welfare of beings, And to that which is the conduct of the heroic ones.
examples.gm: Having established supreme joy, respect, and faith, Having removed obscurations and afflictions and passed beyond stains, The perfection of wisdom of the gentle ones engaged in the benefit of beings, Listen to that in which the heroes practice.
examples.sa: पर प्रेम गौरव प्रसाद उपस्थपित्वा प्रजहित्व आवरण क्लेशमलातिक्रान्ताः । शृणुता जगार्थमभिप्रस्थित सुरव्रतानां प्रज्ञाय पारमित यत्र चरन्ति शूराः ॥

examples.dm: For example, a skillful person endowed with all excellent qualities, Who is powerful, invincible, diligent, and knowledgeable in the techniques of the arts, Who has mastered archery and many other fields of craftsmanship, And who, knowing how to perform illusions, greatly desires the welfare of beings—
examples.gm: For example, a skilled person endowed with all qualities, Powerful, invincible, having made effort, knowing the rites of arts, Who has reached the far shore of archery and many crafts, Knowing how to conjure illusions, intensely desiring the welfare of beings,
examples.sa: पुरुषो यथा कुशल सर्वगुणैरुपेतो बलवान् दुधर्षु कृतयोग्य कलाविधिज्ञो । इष्वस्त्रपारमिगतो पृथुशिल्पयुक्तो मायाविधिज्ञपरमो जगदर्थकामो ॥

examples.dm: Whether one dwells in a town or in a forest, If one is free from the mind of the two vehicles and is certain of supreme enlightenment, This is the solitude of those who have entered into the service of beings; Any bodhisattva who feels superior to them has degraded themselves.
examples.gm: Whether abiding in a village or else in an isolated monastery, If free from the minds of the two vehicles and certain of supreme awakening, This is the solitude of those engaged in the benefit of beings; That conceited bodhisattva ruins themselves.
examples.sa: ग्रामान्ति यो विहरते अथवा अरण्ये द्वययानचित्तविगतो नियतोऽग्रबोधिम् । एषो विवेकु जगदर्थभिप्रस्थितानां आत्मा क्षिणोति तुलयेय स बोधिसत्त्वो ॥

examples.dm: Why is that? Because those supreme speakers, having trained in this, Here demonstrate that all phenomena are emptiness. Having heard that, the Hearers quickly reach liberation, And they reach the awakening of Pratyekabuddhas and the awakening of Buddhas.
examples.gm: If asked why: those supreme speakers, having trained in this, Demonstrate all dharmas here as emptiness. Hearing that, śrāvakas swiftly touch complete liberation, And touch the awakening of pratyekabuddhas and the awakening of buddhas.
examples.sa: किं कारणं त इह शिक्षित वादिश्रेष्ठा गमयन्ति धर्म निखिलानिह शून्यतायाम् । यां श्रुत्व श्रावक स्पृशन्ति विमुक्ति शीघ्रं प्रत्येकबोधि स्पृशयन्ति च बुद्धबोधिम् ॥

examples.dm: Likewise, those who have truly entered into supreme awakening should understand that by hearing This Perfection of Wisdom of the Victors, Even if they have not received a direct prophecy from the Guide, "Before long, I shall touch the awakening of a Buddha."
examples.gm: Likewise, one who has fully entered supreme enlightenment Should be known as hearing this perfection of wisdom of the Victors; Even if they have not been directly prophesied by the Leaders, They think, 'Before long, I will touch the enlightenment of the Buddhas.'
examples.sa: एमेव बोधिवरप्रस्थितु वेदितव्यो श्रुणमाण प्रज्ञ इमि पारमिता जिनानाम् । यद्यापि संमुख न व्याकृतु नायकेनो तथपि स्पृशिष्यति नचिरेण हु बुद्धबोधिम् ॥

examples.dm: Bodhisattvas who have entered the supreme awakening of a Buddha Should rely on the perfections as their spiritual friends. Those who provide such instruction are the ground of accomplishment; Through these two causes, the awakening of a Buddha is swiftly realized.
examples.gm: Bodhisattvas entered into the supreme awakening of a Buddha Should rely on spiritual friends together with the perfections. Those who teach accordingly, this is the stage of accomplishment; By these two causes, they will swiftly realize the awakening of a Buddha.
examples.sa: बुद्धा य बोधिवरप्रस्थित बोधिसत्त्वा कल्याणमित्र इमि पारमिता निदिष्टाः । ते चानुशासक इयं प्रतिपत्तिभूमी दुवि कारणेन अनुबुध्यति बुद्धबोधिम् ॥

examples.dm: While practicing the dharmas of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, They do not touch upon nirvāṇa, yet do not engage in signs; For example, just as a skilled boatman goes back and forth, Without staying on either shore and without remaining in the ocean.
examples.gm: Practicing the dharmas of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, Not touching nirvāṇa and not engaging in signs, Just as a skilled boatman going back and forth, Does not dwell on either shore, nor does he dwell in the ocean.
examples.sa: शून्यानिमित्तप्रणिधिं चरमाणु धर्मा न च निर्वृतिं स्पृशति नो च निमित्तचारी । यथ नाविको कुशल गच्छति आरपारम् उभयान्ति अस्थितु न तिष्ठति अर्णवेस्मिन् ॥

examples.dm: Likewise, the wise bodhisattva abides in compassion, Having fully taken up the two umbrellas of skillful means and wisdom; They contemplate all phenomena as empty, signless, and wishless, And without touching nirvana, they also perceive the true nature of phenomena.
examples.gm: Likewise, a skilled bodhisattva dwelling in compassion, Completely holding the two umbrellas of skillful means and wisdom, Realizing that dharmas are empty, signless, and wishless, Does not touch nirvāṇa, yet sees the dharmas.
examples.sa: एमेव स्थित्व करुणां विदु बोधिसत्त्वो प्रज्ञाउपायद्वयछत्रपरिगृहीतो । शून्यानिमित्तप्रणिधिं विमृषाति धर्मान् न च निर्वृतिं स्पृशति पश्यति धर्मचारी ॥

examples.dm: When, having connected with beings through loving-kindness, He practices the meditative stabilizations of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, It is impossible to designate that he has attained nirvana, Or to designate him as something conditioned; he does not abide anywhere.
examples.gm: Whenever, having bound themselves with love for wanderers, They practice the samādhis of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, Can it be designated that they will attain nirvāṇa, Or that they are conditioned? They have no abiding.
examples.sa: यं कालि मैत्रि जगती अनुबन्धयित्वा शून्यानिमित्तप्रणिधी चरते समाधिम् । अस्थानमेव यदि निर्वृति प्रापुणेया अथवापि संस्कृत स प्रज्ञपनाय शक्यः ॥

examples.dm: Teaching of omniscience
examples.gm: Teaching on the Knowledge of All Aspects

examples.dm: The first chapter teaches omniscience of all aspects. Whatever rivers flow here in Jambudvīpa, Producing flowers, fruits, medicinal plants, and forests, All depend upon the Naga King, the Lord of Nagas, who dwells in Anavatapta; They are the power and glory of that Lord of Nagas.
examples.gm: Chapter One: The Teaching on the Knowledge of All Aspects. However many rivers flow in this Jambudvīpa, Producing flowers, fruits, medicinal herbs, and forests, All depend upon the nāga king, the lord of nāgas, dwelling in Anavatapta; It is the majestic power of that lord of nāgas.
examples.sa: यावन्ति नद्य प्रवहन्ति ह जम्बुद्वीपे फल पुष्प औषधाधि वनस्पति रोहयन्ति । भूजत गजेन्द्रनागपतिनिश्रयनोवतनस्य तस्यानुभावश्रिय साभु जगाधिपस्य ॥

examples.dm: These four types of persons are not afraid of that: The Child of the Victors skilled in the truths, the irreversible one, The Arhat who has cleared away stains and abandoned doubt, And fourth, the one who is fully embraced by a spiritual friend.
examples.gm: These four kinds of persons are not terrified by this: The children of the Victorious One who are wise in the truth, those who are irreversible, Arhats who have cleared away stains and abandoned doubt, And fourth, those perfectly embraced by spiritual friends.
examples.sa: चत्वारि पुद्गल इमे न त्रसन्ति येऽस्मिन् जिनपुत्र सत्यकुशलो अविवर्तियश्च । अर्हं विधूतमलक्लेश प्रहीणकाङ्क्षो कल्याणमित्रपरिपाचित यश्चतुर्थः ॥

examples.dm: For the sake of other beings and persons, the bodhisattva of pure intention Applies themselves with diligent exertion to the perfection of perseverance. For example, just as a female slave carrying water is powerless and under the control of her master, So too do the heroic beings proceed under the control of all sentient beings.
examples.gm: For the sake of other sentient beings and persons, the perfectly pure bodhisattva Manifestly exerts themselves and acts in the perfection of diligence; For example, a servant woman drawing water has no power of her own, but is under the power of her master; Similarly, the heroes act under the power of all sentient beings.
examples.sa: परसत्त्वपुद्गलनिदान विशुद्धसत्त्वा विचरन्ति वीर्यबलपारमिताभियुक्ताः । यथ कुम्भदासि अवशावश भर्तिकस्य तथ सर्वसत्त्ववशतामुपयान्ति धीराः ॥

examples.dm: Just as seeds that are sown and remain in the earth will eventually grow, Once the assembly of conditions is found, diverse forms are fully produced; The five perfections and however many qualities of awakening there are, All of them are born from the perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Seeds, having been sown and resting in the earth, will arise; Having found the proper conditions, many kinds of forms are fully produced. The five perfections and however many qualities of awakening there are, All of them also are produced from the perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: बीजाः प्रकीर्ण पृथिवीस्थित संभवन्ति सामग्रि लब्ध्व विरुहन्ति अनेकरुपाः । यावन्ति बोधिगुण पारमिताश् च पञ्च प्रज्ञाय पारमित ते विरुहन्ति सर्वे ॥

examples.dm: The great beings exist solely to bring sentient beings to maturity, To purify the fields, and to complete the perfections; They do not seek rebirth in the formless realm, thinking That the qualities of enlightenment and the perfections would thereby decline.
examples.gm: The great beings, to completely ripen sentient beings, Act only to purify the realms and complete the perfections; Thinking, "The qualities of awakening and the perfections will diminish," They do not seek birth in the formless realm.
examples.sa: अन्यत्र सत्त्वपरिपाचन क्षेत्रशोधी परिपूरणार्थ इमि पारमिता महात्मा । आरूप्यधातुउपपत्ति न प्रार्थयन्ती यत्रेह बोधिगुणपारमितान हानि ॥

examples.dm: Likewise, those who have truly entered into supreme awakening should understand that by hearing This Perfection of Wisdom of the Victors, Even if they have not received a direct prophecy from the Guide, "Before long, I shall touch the awakening of a Buddha."
examples.gm: Likewise, one who has fully entered supreme enlightenment Should be known as hearing this perfection of wisdom of the Victors; Even if they have not been directly prophesied by the Leaders, They think, 'Before long, I will touch the enlightenment of the Buddhas.'
examples.sa: एमेव बोधिवरप्रस्थितु वेदितव्यो श्रुणमाण प्रज्ञ इमि पारमिता जिनानाम् । यद्यापि संमुख न व्याकृतु नायकेनो तथपि स्पृशिष्यति नचिरेण हु बुद्धबोधिम् ॥

examples.dm: Therefore, those who seek supreme enlightenment, Being wise and possessing intense resolve, should utterly conquer pride; Just as a multitude of the sick rely on a physician for healing, One should rely on a spiritual friend without any distraction.
examples.gm: Therefore, one who seeks holy awakening, A wise one possessing strong intention, having definitely destroyed pride, Just as a multitude of sick people rely on a doctor to be cured, Should rely on spiritual friends without wavering.
examples.sa: तस्मा हु मानु निहनित्वन पण्डितेन गुरुआशयेन वरबोधि गवेषमाणः । वैद्यो व आतुर स्वरोगचिकित्सनार्थं कल्याणमित्र भजितव्य अतन्द्रितेन ॥

examples.dm: They do not act as diviners, predicting whether those engaged in desire will have a boy or a girl. They strive in the supreme perfection of wisdom, which is utterly secluded, free from strife and contention, and their minds of loving-kindness are firm. Desiring omniscience, they are steadfast and possess a mind constantly dedicated to it.
examples.gm: They do not predict, saying, 'You will become a man or a woman engaged in actions of desire.' In the utterly isolated perfection of wisdom, they are free from conflict and dispute, and their mind of loving-kindness is firm. Desiring omniscience, they are steadfast and always endowed with a mind inclined toward it.
examples.sa: न च आदिशन्ति पुरुषैः स्त्रिय इच्छकर्मां प्रविविक्त प्रज्ञवरपारमिताभियुक्ताः । कलहाविवादविगता दृढमैत्रचित्ता सर्वज्ञकाम सद शासनि निम्नचित्ताः ॥

examples.dm: Even if a bodhisattva indulges in the five objects of sensory desire, If they have gone for refuge to the Buddha, the Dharma, and the noble Sangha, And maintain the mental orientation toward omniscience, thinking, "I must achieve buddhahood," The wise should understand that they abide in the perfection of ethical discipline.
examples.gm: Even if a bodhisattva enjoys the five sensory pleasures, If they have taken refuge in the Buddha, Dharma, and the noble Sangha, And direct their mind toward omniscience, thinking, "I will accomplish buddhahood!" The wise one should be known as abiding in the perfection of discipline.
examples.sa: यदि पञ्च कामगुण भुञ्जति बोधिसत्त्वो बुद्धं च धर्म शरणागतु आर्यसंघम् । सर्वज्ञता च मनसी भविष्यामि बुद्धो स्थितु शीलपारमित वेदयितव्य विज्ञो ॥

examples.dm: The many spirits and diseases in the human world Are pacified through the blessing of truth by those endowed with benefit and compassion; Yet they remain without conceit and do not give rise to pride— One should understand that this is the prophecy of non-retrogression.
examples.gm: In the human world, there are many bhūta demons and diseases; Possessing benefit and compassion, they pacify them through the blessing of truth. Yet they have no conceit and do not produce pride; They should be known as irreversible and prophesied.
examples.sa: भूतग्रहा विविध व्याधय मर्त्यलोके सत्याधिष्ठानि प्रशमेति हितानुकम्पी । न च तेन मन्यन् उपपद्यति नापि मानम् अविवर्तियेति अयु व्याकृतु वेदितव्यः ॥

examples.dm: Therefore, those who seek supreme enlightenment, Being wise and possessing intense resolve, should utterly conquer pride; Just as a multitude of the sick rely on a physician for healing, One should rely on a spiritual friend without any distraction.
examples.gm: Therefore, one who seeks holy awakening, A wise one possessing strong intention, having definitely destroyed pride, Just as a multitude of sick people rely on a doctor to be cured, Should rely on spiritual friends without wavering.
examples.sa: तस्मा हु मानु निहनित्वन पण्डितेन गुरुआशयेन वरबोधि गवेषमाणः । वैद्यो व आतुर स्वरोगचिकित्सनार्थं कल्याणमित्र भजितव्य अतन्द्रितेन ॥

examples.dm: If, with the thought, "I shall bring all beings to maturity and act for their benefit," One applies oneself with body, speech, and mind, Yet remains dwelling in the perception of a self, one has become lazy; They are as far from omniscience as the earth is from the sky.
examples.gm: Thinking, "Having completely ripened beings, I will act for their benefit," If they exert themselves with body, speech, and mind, Because they abide in the perception of a self, they have become lazy, And they become as far from omniscience as the sky is from the earth.
examples.sa: सचि कायचित्तवचसा च पराक्रमेय्या परिपाचयित्व जगती करिष्यामि अर्थम् । कौसीद्यप्राप्त भवती स्थितु आत्मसंज्ञैः नैरात्मभावनविदूरि नभं व भूमेः ॥

examples.dm: Those who grasp at the actual perception of a self and hold things as "mine" are attached; How could fools like these ever have the intention to give? Those who are stingy will be born in the realm of hungry ghosts; Even if they are born as humans, they will be destitute at that time.
examples.gm: Perceiving a self, one is attached to things through grasping them as "mine"; How could fools have the mind of generosity? Miserly ones will be born in the realm of hungry ghosts; Or even if they are born as humans, they will then be impoverished.
examples.sa: अहसंज्ञतस्तु ममता भवते च रागो कुतु त्यागबुद्धि भविष्यति सा मुहानाम् । मात्सर्य प्रेत भवते उपपद्ययाती अथवा मनुष्य तद भोति दरिद्ररूपो ॥

examples.dm: In the language of India: Ārya-prajñāpāramitā-sañcayagāthā. In the language of Tibet: 'Phags pa shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa sdud pa tshigs su bcad pa. Homage to the Noble Mañjuśrī!
examples.gm: In the language of India: Āryaprajñāpāramitāsañcayagāthā. In the language of Tibet: The Noble Verse Summary of the Perfection of Wisdom. Homage to the noble Mañjuśrī.
examples.sa: ओम् नमो भगवत्यै आर्यप्रज्ञापारमितारत्नगुणसंचयगाथायै । नमो आर्यमञ्जुश्रिये ।

examples.dm: Any bodhisattva who abides here in peace in this way, Has been prophesied by the Tathāgatas of the past. They have no conceit of thinking, "I am in meditative equipoise," or "I have arisen," Why is that? Because the nature of phenomena is fully understood.
examples.gm: Whatever bodhisattva dwells here thus in peace, Is prophesied by the Tathāgatas of the past. They have no conceited thought, "I am in meditative equipoise" or "I have arisen." Why is this? Because they completely understand the nature of phenomena.
examples.sa: एवात्मशान्ति विहरन्निह बोधिसत्त्वो सो व्याकृतो पुरमकेहि तथागतेहि । न च मन्यते अहु समाधितु व्युत्थितो वा कस्मार्थ धर्मप्रकृतिं परिजानयित्वा ॥

examples.dm: If one asks, "Why is this called the Great Vehicle of Awakening?" It is because by mounting it, one delivers all sentient beings from suffering. This vehicle is a vast celestial palace, as immense as space; It is the supreme vehicle, the means for fully attaining joy, delight, and bliss.
examples.gm: Why is this called the Great Vehicle of Awakening? Mounting it, all sentient beings pass beyond sorrow. This vehicle is a great immeasurable palace like space, The supreme vehicle, which brings about the attainment of joy, happiness, and bliss.
examples.sa: किं कारणं अयु प्रवुच्यति बोधियानो यत्रारुहित्व स निर्वापयि सर्वसत्त्वान् । आकाशतुल्य अयु यान महाविमानो सुखसौख्यक्षेमभिप्रापणु यानश्रेष्ठो ॥

examples.dm: These four types of persons are not afraid of that: The Child of the Victors skilled in the truths, the irreversible one, The Arhat who has cleared away stains and abandoned doubt, And fourth, the one who is fully embraced by a spiritual friend.
examples.gm: These four kinds of persons are not terrified by this: The children of the Victorious One who are wise in the truth, those who are irreversible, Arhats who have cleared away stains and abandoned doubt, And fourth, those perfectly embraced by spiritual friends.
examples.sa: चत्वारि पुद्गल इमे न त्रसन्ति येऽस्मिन् जिनपुत्र सत्यकुशलो अविवर्तियश्च । अर्हं विधूतमलक्लेश प्रहीणकाङ्क्षो कल्याणमित्रपरिपाचित यश्चतुर्थः ॥

examples.dm: Yet someone were to write down in a book this Mother of the Sugatas, From whom the Ten Powers of the Guides arise, And, bearing it, were to honor it with flowers and ointments, The merit of having worshiped stūpas would not approach even a fraction of that.
examples.gm: Whoever, regarding that from which the Guides of ten powers will arise, Writes this Mother of the Sugatas in a book, Retains it, and pays reverence with flowers and ointments, The merit of building stūpas and making offerings cannot match a fraction of that.
examples.sa: यश् चो इमां सुगतमात लिखित्व पुस्ते यत उत्पती दशबलान विनायकानाम् । धारेयि सत्करयि पुष्पविलेपनेहि कल पुण्य भोन्ति न स स्तूपि करित्व पूजाम् ॥

examples.dm: Wisdom is the precursor to the practice of generosity, And likewise for ethical discipline, patience, diligence, and meditative concentration. It is the total sustainer that prevents virtuous qualities from being lost; This demonstrates the single nature of all phenomena.
examples.gm: Wisdom is what precedes giving; Ethical discipline, patience, joyous effort, and concentration are likewise. In order that virtuous dharmas are not wasted, it fully upholds them. This demonstrates all dharmas as having a single way.
examples.sa: पूर्वंगमा भवतु दानु ददन्तु प्रज्ञा शीले च क्षान्ति तथ वीर्य तथैव ध्याने । परिग्राहिका कुशलधर्म-अविप्रणाशे एका च सा अपि निदर्शयि सर्वधर्मान् ॥

examples.dm: From the time they first generate the aspiration for supreme enlightenment, Until the time the true Dharma of those guides is exhausted, Whatever merit those Victors possess during that interval, Including the perfections and all the Buddha-qualities,
examples.gm: From when they first generated the mind for supreme awakening, Until the time the holy dharma of those Guides is exhausted, Whatever merit those Victors have during that time, And whatever is endowed with the perfections and whatever buddha-dharmas—
examples.sa: प्रथमं उपादु वरबोधयि चित्तुपादो यावत् सु धर्मक्षयकालु विनायकानाम् । एकस्मि तत्र चिय तेष जिनान पुण्यं सह युक्त पारमित येऽपि च बुद्धधर्माः ॥

examples.dm: Even if one has honored billions of Buddhas in former lives, If one lacks faith in the Victors' perfection of wisdom, That person of small intelligence, upon hearing it, will reject it; Having rejected it, they become defenseless and go to the Unrelenting Hell.
examples.gm: Even if they honored hundreds of billions of buddhas when practicing previously, If they do not have faith in the perfection of wisdom of the Victors, Upon hearing it, those of small intelligence will abandon it; Having abandoned it, becoming without refuge, they go to the Avīci hell.
examples.sa: सत्कृत्य बुद्धनियुतां परिचारिकायां न च प्रज्ञपारमित श्रद्दधिता जिनानाम् । श्रुत्वा च सो इमु क्षिपिष्यति सोऽल्पबुद्धिः स क्षिपित्व यास्यति अवीचिम् अत्राणभूतो ॥

examples.dm: The fourth chapter explains the complete realization of all aspects. Śakra, the king of the gods, asked the Victor: "How do Bodhisattvas practicing wisdom apply diligence?" "They do not apply even a particle of diligence toward the aggregates or the elements; Not applying diligence toward the aggregates is the Bodhisattva's diligence."
examples.gm: The fourth chapter: teaching the complete realization of all aspects. The king of gods, Śakra, asked the Victor: "How does a bodhisattva strive in the practice of wisdom?" "They do not strive even a speck of dust in the aggregates and elements; Not striving in the aggregates, that is the striving of a bodhisattva."
examples.sa: शक्रो जिनस्य परिपृच्छति देवराजो चरमाण प्रज्ञ कथ युज्यति बोधिसत्त्वो । अणुमात्र यो न खलु युज्यति स्कन्धधातौ यो एव युज्यति स युज्यति बोधिसत्त्वः ॥

examples.dm: Those who, at that time, have become longing and faithful, Having gone to listen to this sublime Dharma, Once they perceive the Dharma preacher to be preoccupied, They will depart without joy and with a troubled mind.
examples.gm: Those who at that time, having become eager and faithful, Go to listen to this holy dharma, Upon knowing that the speaker of dharma is busy with activities, Will depart, devoid of joy and unhappy.
examples.sa: ये चापि तस्मि समये इमु धर्म श्रेष्ठं श्रुणनाय छन्दिक उत्पादयिष्यन्ति श्रद्धाम् । ते धर्मभाणक विदित्वन कार्ययुक्तं प्रेमापनीत गमिष्यन्ति सुदुर्मनाश्च ॥

examples.dm: For example, just as a lion dwelling in a mountain glen is fearless, And its roar strikes terror into many small wild animals, So too the Lion among men, by relying on the Perfection of Wisdom, Terrifies the many non-Buddhists and lets out his roar throughout the world.
examples.gm: For example, just as a fearless lion dwelling in a mountain ravine Terrifies many small wild animals and lets out a roar, The lion of men, relying on the perfection of wisdom, Terrifies many tīrthikas and also lets out a roar in the world.
examples.sa: सिंहो यथैव गिरिकन्दरि निश्रयित्वा नदते अछम्भि मृग क्षुद्रक त्रासयन्तो । तथ प्रज्ञपारमितनिश्रय नराण सिंहो नदते अछम्भि पृथुतीर्थिक त्रासयन्तो ॥

examples.dm: For those bodhisattvas who abide on the level of a beginner, And have entered into the supreme awakening of a Buddha with a resolute intention, Those excellent students who possess devotion for their gurus Should always rely upon wise masters.
examples.gm: Any bodhisattva abiding on the ground of a beginner, Who has set out for the supreme enlightenment of a Buddha with a pure intention, As good disciples possessing devotion to their guru, They should always rely on wise gurus.
examples.sa: यो आदिकर्म स्थितु भूमिय बोधिसत्त्वो अध्याशयेन वर प्रस्थित बुद्धबोधिम् । तेही सुशिष्यगुरुगौरवसंप्रयुक्तो कल्याणमित्र सद सेवयितव्य विज्ञैः ॥

examples.dm: Those who possess such qualities are free from conceptual elaboration; Free from doubt, hesitation, and uncertainty, they are endowed with the true meaning. Having heard the perfection of wisdom, they do not shrink back; They do not rely on others and should be known as irreversible.
examples.gm: They are endowed with such dharmas and are free from conceptual proliferation. They are free from doubt, hesitation, and wavering, and possess the ultimate meaning. Those who, having heard the perfection of wisdom, do not shrink back, Should be known as irreversible and not reliant on others.
examples.sa: ते एव धर्मसमुदागत निष्प्रपञ्चा काङ्क्षाविलेखविमतीविगतार्थयुक्ताः । प्रज्ञाय पारमित श्रुत्व न सीदयन्ति अपरप्रणेय अविवर्तिय वेदितव्याः ॥

examples.dm: They are free from the perception of diversity and speak words consistent with reason; They do not rely on other śramaṇas or brahmins. These wise ones have forever abandoned the three lower realms; They are intensely devoted to the paths of the ten virtuous actions.
examples.gm: Free from differentiated perceptions and speaking rational words, Not relying on other śramaṇas and brahmins; The wise always abandon the three lower realms at all times, And vividly strive in the path of the ten virtuous actions.
examples.sa: नानात्वसंज्ञविगता गिर युक्तभाणी न च अन्य ते श्रमण ब्राह्मण आश्रयन्ति । त्रियपायवर्जित विदू सदकालि भोन्ति दशभिश् च ते कुशलकर्मपथेभि युक्ता ॥

examples.dm: Whatever is called the perfection of the Victors, Those phenomena are also proclaimed to be merely names. A bodhisattva who dedicates without conceptual arrogance Will not decline and will touch the supreme awakening of a Buddha.
examples.gm: Whatever is called the perfection of the victors, Those dharmas too are fully proclaimed to be merely names. A bodhisattva who fully dedicates without a conceited mind Will without decline touch the supreme awakening of a buddha.
examples.sa: ये चापि पञ्च इमि पारमिता जिनानाम् एतेऽपि धर्म परिकीर्तित नाममात्राः । परिणामयाति न च मन्यति बोधिसत्त्वो न च हीयते स्पृशति उत्तमबुद्धबोधिम् ॥

examples.dm: Or if, because they have acquired various blessings of truth, They develop conceit, thinking, "I have been prophesied," Or if they become conceited because other bodhisattvas have received a prophecy, Know that those who abide in such conceit are of small intelligence.
examples.gm: However, if through those various blessings of truth Being accomplished, the conceit arises thinking, "I am prophesied," Or if a bodhisattva is conceited about being prophesied by another, Abiding in conceit, they should be known as having small intelligence.
examples.sa: अथवास्य मन्यन् उपपद्यति व्याकृतोऽस्मि सत्याधिष्ठान विविधानि समृद्ध्ययन्ति । यदि अन्य व्याकृतकु मन्यति बोधिसत्त्वो ज्ञातव्य मन्यनस्थितो अयु अल्पबुद्धिः ॥

examples.dm: For all the Victors of the past, the future, and those residing in the ten directions, This perfection is the path; there is no other. This perfection is said to be the clarity, the lamp, the light, And the supreme guide for those who have entered upon supreme enlightenment.
examples.gm: The Victorious Ones of the past, future, and whoever abide in the ten directions, The path of all of them is this perfection, and no other. This perfection is, for those entered into supreme awakening, Explained as the supreme illumination, lamp, light, and teacher.
examples.sa: अतिक्रान्तनागत जिना स्थित ये दिशासु सर्वेषु मार्गु अयु पारमिता अनन्यो । ओभास उल्क वरबोधयि प्रस्थितानाम् आलोक शास्त्रि इमि पारमिता प्रदिष्टाः ॥

examples.dm: Any bodhisattva who has long been connected to this, In order to liberate beings of the heavens, the human realm, and the three lower realms, And who desires to show the vast path to the realm of beings on the other side, Should day and night apply themselves to the perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Any bodhisattva who, for the sake of liberating The sentient beings of gods, humans, and the three lower realms bound here for a long time, Desires to teach the broad path to the other shore to the realm of beings, Should strive in the perfection of wisdom day and night.
examples.sa: चिरबुद्धदेवमनुजान् त्रिअपायि सत्त्वान् परिमोचितुं य इह इच्छति बोधिसत्त्वो । पृथुमार्गु तीरु उपदर्शयि सत्त्वधातौ प्रज्ञाय पारमित युक्त दिवा च रात्रौ ॥

examples.dm: When training, one does not make any claims about the training; One does not perceive a trainee or the qualities to be trained in, And does not conceptualize between training and non-training— Whoever trains in this way trains here in these Buddha-qualities.
examples.gm: When training, whoever does not assert any training, And does not observe the trainer or the dharmas of training, And does not conceptualize these two: having trained and not having trained, Whoever trains like that, trains in this Dharma of the Buddhas.
examples.sa: यो शिक्षमाणु न उपैति कहिंचि शिक्षां न च शिक्षकं लभति नापि च शिक्षधर्मान् । शिक्षा अशिक्ष उभयो अविकल्पमानो यो शिक्षते स इह शिक्षति बुद्धधर्मे ॥

examples.dm: Those who have entered into the supreme, irreversible awakening, Rejoice from the depths of their hearts in the generation of the mind of enlightenment; Though one might find the measure of the three thousandfold world system and Mount Meru by weighing them on a scale, The virtue of such rejoicing is not like that.
examples.gm: Regarding those who have fully entered supreme, irreversible awakening, Rejoicing from the depths of one's heart in their generation of the mind— The Mount Meru of a trichiliocosm could be measured by weighing it on a scale, But the virtue of that rejoicing is not like that.
examples.sa: अविवर्तियस्य वरबोधयि प्रस्थितस्य यो चित्तुपादु अनुमोदितु आशयेन । त्रिसहस्र मेरु तुलयित्व सियाप्रमाणो न त्वेव तस्य कुशलस्यनुमोदनाये ॥

examples.dm: To those who practice skillfully in this way, the many hosts of gods Join their palms in reverence and prostrate. All the Buddhas throughout the world systems of the ten directions Likewise utter garlands of praise for their qualities.
examples.gm: To the wise who practice thus, many hosts of gods Join their palms, bow down, and pay homage; And however many Buddhas there are in the world systems of the ten directions, They completely proclaim a garland of praise for their qualities.
examples.sa: एवं चरन्तु विदु ना पृथुदेवसंघाः कृतअञ्जलीपुट प्रणम्य नमस्ययन्ति । बुद्धा पि यावत दशद्दिशि लोकधातौ गुणवर्णमालपरिकीर्तन कुर्वयन्ति ॥

examples.dm: However many aspects of primordial wisdom, gateways, methods, and roots there may be, All these arise from the supreme Perfection of Wisdom. When conditions assemble, the machine of karma fully emerges; In the Perfection of Wisdom, there is no exhaustion and no increase.
examples.gm: However many approaches to knowledge, methods, and roots there are, They all arise from the supreme perfection of wisdom; When conditions come together, the machine of activities perfectly arises, Yet the perfection of wisdom has no exhaustion and no increase.
examples.sa: यावन्ति ज्ञान नयद्वार उयायमूलाः सर्वे ति प्रज्ञवरपारमिताप्रसूताः । सामग्रिप्रत्यय प्रवर्तति ज्ञानयन्त्रो न च प्रज्ञपारमित वर्धति हीयते वा ॥

examples.dm: The great beings exist solely to bring sentient beings to maturity, To purify the fields, and to complete the perfections; They do not seek rebirth in the formless realm, thinking That the qualities of enlightenment and the perfections would thereby decline.
examples.gm: The great beings, to completely ripen sentient beings, Act only to purify the realms and complete the perfections; Thinking, "The qualities of awakening and the perfections will diminish," They do not seek birth in the formless realm.
examples.sa: अन्यत्र सत्त्वपरिपाचन क्षेत्रशोधी परिपूरणार्थ इमि पारमिता महात्मा । आरूप्यधातुउपपत्ति न प्रार्थयन्ती यत्रेह बोधिगुणपारमितान हानि ॥

examples.dm: For the sake of other beings and persons, the bodhisattva of pure intention Applies themselves with diligent exertion to the perfection of perseverance. For example, just as a female slave carrying water is powerless and under the control of her master, So too do the heroic beings proceed under the control of all sentient beings.
examples.gm: For the sake of other sentient beings and persons, the perfectly pure bodhisattva Manifestly exerts themselves and acts in the perfection of diligence; For example, a servant woman drawing water has no power of her own, but is under the power of her master; Similarly, the heroes act under the power of all sentient beings.
examples.sa: परसत्त्वपुद्गलनिदान विशुद्धसत्त्वा विचरन्ति वीर्यबलपारमिताभियुक्ताः । यथ कुम्भदासि अवशावश भर्तिकस्य तथ सर्वसत्त्ववशतामुपयान्ति धीराः ॥

examples.dm: Any bodhisattva who possesses the excellent quality of patience— Suppose someone were to fill the three thousandfold world system with jewels and offer them to the Knower of the World, To the Buddhas, Arhats, and Pratyekabuddhas; The mass of merit from that giving would not equal even a fraction of this.
examples.gm: Whatever bodhisattva is endowed with the excellent dharma of patience, Compared to someone who fills the three thousandfold world system with jewels and offers them to the Knowers of the World, The Buddhas, arhats, and solitary realizers, That mass of generosity cannot match a fraction of the merit of the former.
examples.sa: सो बोधिसत्त्व क्षमते गुणधर्मयुक्तो यश् चैव रत्नभरितं त्रिसहस्र दद्यात् । बुद्धान लोकविदुनार्हतप्रत्ययानां कलपुण्य सो न भवते इह दानस्कन्धे ॥

examples.dm: If a bodhisattva practicing the path of the Victors thinks, "These sentient beings are ethical, but those are unethical," Engaging in such diverse perceptions, they are utterly lacking in ethical discipline; Their morality has degenerated, and they lack completely purified morality.
examples.gm: If a bodhisattva practicing the path of the Victorious Ones Thinks, "These sentient beings have discipline; these have broken discipline," By engaging in such diverse perceptions, their discipline is completely broken; Their discipline degenerates, and they lack completely pure discipline.
examples.sa: यदि बोधिसत्त्व चरमाणु जिनान मार्गे इमि शीलवानिमि दुशील करोति सत्त्वान् । नानात्वसंज्ञप्रसृतो परमं दुशीलो अपि छिद्रशीलु न तु सो परिशुद्धशीलो ॥

examples.dm: At that time, the bodhisattva, knowing that sentient beings are impoverished, Will take delight in generosity and always give with great excellence. They feel more joy from giving away the four continents, beautifully adorned, as if they were a glob of spittle, Than they would from acquiring those continents.
examples.gm: Then, the bodhisattva, knowing that sentient beings are impoverished, Becomes intent on giving and always gives freely. The four continents, beautifully adorned, are like a glob of spit; Having given them away they become joyful, but attaining the continents is not like that.
examples.sa: तद बोधिसत्त्व इमि ज्ञात्व दरिद्रसत्त्वान् दानाधिमुक्त भवती सद मुक्तत्यागी । चत्वारि द्वीपि समलंकृतु खेटतुल्यं दत्त्वा उदग्र भवते न हि द्वीपलब्धो ॥

examples.dm: Through ethical discipline, one abandons the various states of animal existence, And by abandoning the eight unfree states, one always finds leisure. Through patience, one will attain a sublime, vast, and beautiful form; With a lovely golden complexion, one becomes worthy of being beheld by all beings.
examples.gm: By discipline, the nature of the manifold destinies of animals and The eight unfree states are abandoned, and leisure is always found. By patience, a fine, supreme, and vast form will be obtained, Golden-colored, beautiful, and worthy to be looked at by beings.
examples.sa: शीलेन तीर्यगति वर्जयि नेकरुपाम् अष्टौ च अक्षण क्षणां लभते स नित्यम् । क्षान्तीय रुप लभते परमं उदारं सुवर्णच्छवि प्रियु जगस्य उदीक्षणीयो ॥

examples.dm: The eighth chapter: teaching the Dharmakāya. One fully embraces the pure realm and the purity of sentient beings; One fully embraces the lineage of the Buddha and the lineage of the Dharma; Likewise, one fully embraces the lineage of the Saṅgha and all phenomena.
examples.gm: Chapter Eight: Teaching the Dharmakāya. Fully upholds perfectly pure fields and pure sentient beings; Fully upholds the Buddha lineage and also the Dharma lineage; Likewise fully upholds the Sangha lineage and all dharmas.
